evidence: Same Brooks research archive and overlapping protocol years. The 2011 analysis selects profiles with at least 10% DCS and VGE monitoring and reports 2,077 exposures. The 2010 database manual reports a broader completed-exposure margin of 2,946.
The cited source list includes Brooks protocols appearing in A1309. The 2,077-exposure joint subset cannot be linked or split at individual test level.

Both summarize outcomes from the Brooks archive. The 2011 joint data are selected for availability of Doppler observations and profile DCS incidence, so the overlap count with the loglogistic set is unknown.
Kannan et al. cite Ryles and Pilmanis as analyzing the same Brooks database. Selection and dates differ; no linkable exposure identifiers are given.

Completed target exposures at 231 mmHg with mild exercise, 240-min limit and total 75 or 135 min on oxygen are compatible with several DNT profiles. Kannan groups by total time without reporting the whole staging sequence. Exact common exposures are unresolved.
The 1998 analysis is based on a historic subset of the same Brooks database documented in the 2010 manual. No aggregate counts are added across sources.

The five groups align on target altitude, preoxygenation and broad activity label, and both describe 30 exposures per arm. Four apparent actual percentages agree. The 35,000-ft profile reports 91% in 1999 versus the 2004 published Kaplan–Meier rate of 94%.
The same five protocol profiles appear in NEDU Appendix E as MV-A through MV-E with 30 or 31 exposures. Numerators use NEDU's own outcome denominator and scope.
The original Armstrong VAX archive inventory is an early snapshot of the Brooks programme. The 2010 report describes the later Access version and different counted scopes.
